_comment: Outbound policy for the daily triage, one row per channel. Read by skills/daily-triage/SKILL.md
STEP 5b. This file exists so the send/no-send decision is a LOOKUP, never an inference: asking a
model at 07:00 'is this work or personal?' is exactly the judgement that fails silently and
confidently, and it already failed once — Messenger was misread as personal from display names
when it is in fact JCR treasurer comms.
THE RULE IS UNIFORM: nothing is ever sent by the run that composed it. Every outbound message is
drafted, appears in the closeout in full, and is sent by the NEXT run unless cancelled. `mode`
only decides what happens after that hold expires.
send       — drafted, then sent automatically by the next run after the 12h hold
draft-only — drafted and surfaced for a human to send; never sent by the pipeline
`draft-only` is sometimes policy and sometimes physics — see gmail, where the connector has no
send tool at all. The `reason` field says which, because those are not the same thing and a
future reader will want to know whether flipping the mode is even possible.

ALL CHANNELS ARE CURRENTLY draft-only. Nathan's call: the pipeline composes, a human sends. The deferred-send machinery is retained and tested, so flipping one channel back to `send` is a one-word change — but note that mode is enforced at SEND time, not only at draft time, so flipping a channel to draft-only also stops anything already queued for it.

messenger.reason: Draft-only by Nathan's instruction (2026-08-05): every channel drafts, nothing is sent by the pipeline. Previous reason: JCR treasurer comms — official business.

whatsapp.scope: groups whose topic is society/committee business (DUE, UCTEC and similar). Never a 1:1.
whatsapp.reason: Draft-only by Nathan's instruction (2026-08-05): every channel drafts, nothing is sent by the pipeline. Previous reason: Society business. 1:1 WhatsApp is personal and stays out of scope.

linkedin.reason: Draft-only by Nathan's instruction (2026-08-05): every channel drafts, nothing is sent by the pipeline. Previous reason: Requested twice, explicitly. Enabled on that instruction.
linkedin.risk: HIGHEST of any channel here. Automated messaging breaches LinkedIn's user agreement, they detect it, and this account is reached through mautrix-linkedin — an unofficial cookie session. A ban costs the bridge AND the account. Flip to draft-only if that trade stops looking worth it.

instagram.reason: Policy, not capability. Nathan's earlier split was explicit: send on work channels, 'reading and drafting personal messages' only. Instagram is personal. One word here flips it to send.

gmessages.reason: Policy. SMS reaches people who never opted into being messaged by software, and there is no thread context to judge tone from.

discord.reason: Policy. Discord bans aggressively for user-token automation, and outbound is the detectable part. Reading is already the risk being accepted.

gmail.reason: PHYSICS, not policy. The Gmail connector exposes create_draft/update_draft/list_drafts and no send tool of any kind — verified against the live tool list. A draft is created in Gmail and Nathan sends it. Deferred send would need a different transport (SMTP, or the Gmail API with a send scope), which is a separate piece of work.
